body:
# Independent audit: every cubic-tight strict triangle has inward ear variation

Source audited in full, Sections 1--6:
`candidate 3d7872ba08080216`.
Result: **PASS**, without repairs. The retained conclusion is strict first
variation for each fixed nonzero outward triangular ear with an interior
peak. It is not finite-ear monotonicity or a global quadrilateral theorem.

## 1. Actual shape derivative and its section atoms

The edge coordinates P(t)+r w have absolute area Jacobian one with the
stated outward vector. For a fixed Lipschitz roof, cap-area first
variations are integrals of h over its actual signature intervals; movement
of a crossing changes those integrals only by O(epsilon^2). At a crossing
of the line of normal v, write its equation as A(t-t0)+Br=0, where
A=v dot(P_j-P_i) is nonzero. Coarea in these determinant-one coordinates
shows that the section derivative is exactly h(t0)/|A|. This remains valid
when the roof peak is at the crossing, because h is continuous and
Lipschitz. Thus precisely the two stated point masses account for every
section change.

For completeness, the section derivative of the cubic itself is

    partial Psi/partial sigma_l
       =-E_l/sigma_l+C Q_l/(sigma_l^2 M).

This confirms directly that the density coefficients are the raw unique
and double area derivatives holding all sections fixed; the latter alone
would not suffice.

A nearby triangle remains in strict incidence and obeys Psi<=4. Therefore
at a tight triangle all vertex derivatives vanish. At either vertex the
two adjacent edge-normal displacements can indeed be varied independently.
Tangential endpoint shifts create only second-order area corrections and
no first-order contribution at the interior cutting intersections. This
proves the two separate edge moments used in the source.

## 2. An independent exact verification of the moments

Normalize H=1. On edge (i,j), use the source notation p,q,F,G,U,V,
with F=L_is and G=L_js, a=1-V and b=U. Write A_i=2k alpha_i,
A_j=2k alpha_j and B=2k beta_s=A_i+A_j-C.
The actual cap formula gives Q_i/k=a_i^2/(pF), sigma_i=2Q_i/a_i,
and M=1/2. Hence the point masses of the normalized measure 2k nu are

    w_b=F(C-E_i/a_i),    w_a=G(C-E_j/a_j).

Their dimensions and signs follow from the explicit coarea formula above.
Independently expanding the exact p,q,U,V equality data gives both
identities

    A_i a+B(b-a)+A_j(1-b)+w_a+w_b=0,
    A_i a^2/2+B(b^2-a^2)/2+A_j(1-b^2)/2+a w_a+b w_b=0.

These are exactly the zeroth and first moments, and provide a second
verification of all section-normalization factors in the Green proof.

## 3. Green criterion and strict positivity

The kernel min(t,theta)-t theta has distributional second derivative
-minus the point mass at t. Both endpoint values are zero. The two moments
therefore give zero endpoint slopes, yielding the stated negative outer
quadratics. The middle formula has the correct sign: adding
beta_s(b-a)^2 z(1-z)/2 gives second derivative -beta_s.

At Psi=4, positive f implies every f_i<2, and the exact completed-square
identity 4E_i-C f_i^2=P(4-f_i^2)>0 proves alpha_i>0. Dividing the middle
formula by z(1-z) gives precisely the minimization A/z+B/(1-z), with no
omitted endpoint case. Thus inequality (6) is necessary and sufficient,
and its strict version gives a strict derivative at every middle peak.

## 4. Disk inequality

The radical term sqrt(A(r)B(r)) is concave on the full closed interval;
its displayed second derivative is correct, and continuity covers a zero
endpoint. The upper-endpoint identities were independently expanded
symbolically. Their squared difference is strictly negative because all
F,1-F,1-U,1-V,L are positive, so the claimed gap is strictly positive
regardless of the sign of its nonradical part.

At the lower endpoint the two signed roots cannot both be negative.
If both are nonnegative, their sum is strictly less than one, making the
right side strictly negative. If one is negative, the exact relation
b in [L/V,1] is valid, and the affine difference R-Lt has the two stated
strictly positive endpoint values. Since b<=1, its strict positivity pays
the entire right-hand square. These cases exhaust the lower endpoint.
Concavity then gives strict positivity at every intermediate r.

## 5. Equality coordinates and geometric cut locations

The normalized edge drops p,q lie in (0,1): strict off-diagonal margins
and balanced columns give each drop less than the sum of its two positive
vertex margins, hence less than H. The cycle equality gives
F=p(1-q)/D and G=q(1-p)/D, F+G=1. All three squared f entries, P,C,E_i/C
in (9) check exactly.

The actual intersections are a=1-a_j/q and b=a_i/p, so U,V are in (0,1).
The third cap is negative on the whole edge; balanced margins therefore
force a<b, equivalently U+V>1. The parameter r is strictly between zero
and FG because 1-pq-(1-p)(1-q)=D>0. The pyramid formula gives
T_i=f_i/(2a_i) with its exact factor two. Substitution in the raw derivative
produces (10) without an extra scale. Finally beta_s=alpha_i+alpha_j-C/(2k)
because total area is added once, not twice. These facts identify the
actual coupled criterion exactly with the disk inequality.

## 6. Verification and scope

The source checker `supporting computation verify_cubic_ear_disk_certificate_defect_transport.py`
reran successfully: 2,307 exact checks. The independent checker
`supporting computation verify_cubic_ear_atoms_and_disk_audit_slab_recovery.py` additionally verifies
the two actual atom/moment identities symbolically. Numerical or exact-grid
checks are not used as substitutes for the analytic endpoint argument.

No smoothness beyond the polygonal triangle and a fixed Lipschitz roof is
needed. The ordinary cut boundaries carry zero area. For a compact set of
peak parameters away from the vertices the strict margin is uniform by
continuity; no uniform conclusion as a peak approaches a vertex follows
from this note alone. The proof does not assert an (OC) conclusion.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
